paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God is not the problem. The people asked if He had forgotten them, and He answered with questions. "Is My hand too short to redeem you? Or do I lack the strength to deliver you?" (Isaiah 50:2). The trouble was their own sins, not any weakness in Him (Isaiah 50:1).

Then the Servant steps in, and He shows what it looks like to trust God all the way. He listens morning by morning, "I have not been rebellious, nor have I turned back," and He did not hide His face from scorn and spittle (Isaiah 50:5, 6). Why could He stand firm? "Because the Lord GOD helps Me" (Isaiah 50:7). I can't even stand firm when my timer is going off, so I'm taking notes!

Now the question comes to YOU, baker. When you're walking in darkness with no light, the text says, "Let him trust in the name of the LORD; let him lean on his God" (Isaiah 50:10). Lighting your own fire is the other road, and it ends in "a place of torment" (Isaiah 50:11). So lean on Him, listen to the Servant, and let the LORD be your light.
